name: Industrial Machinery Maintenance
description: Industrial maintenance programmes train the people who keep production machinery running — mechanical drives, hydraulics, pneumatics, welding repairs and the electrical controls that tie them together. ⚠ When a line stops, this is who the plant calls, and the pay reflects what a stopped line costs.
degreesNote: The Florida framework is **Industrial Machinery Maintenance and Repair, 1,350 hours across three occupational completion points** — maintenance assistant, then mechanic and technician, then maintenance specialist. ⚠ It is also published as two halves, **750 hours and 600 hours**, so a student can complete the first, go to work, and return for the second. A registered apprenticeship route exists as well, and manufacturers frequently pay for it. ⚠⚠ The programme is taught at only a handful of Florida institutions under the state course numbers — four or five — which is small for an occupation with 45,700 openings a year nationally.

cips.note: Heavy/industrial equipment maintenance technologies — seven Florida public institutions across the series, with industrial machinery maintenance and millwright training the two codes inside it. ⚠ A small recorded footprint for a trade this much in demand, partly because much of the training happens inside employers rather than colleges.

related.note: ⚠ The closest neighbour and an overlapping one: automation and controls is where industrial maintenance is going, and the same colleges teach both. If you enjoy the electrical and control side more than the mechanical, read that one.
Much of a modern breakdown is electrical, and maintenance technicians who can work confidently on controls and motors are the ones plants keep.

⚠ A maintenance technician who can weld is markedly more useful in a breakdown — repair, fabrication and improvisation at three in the morning — and welding is taught at 47 institutions against a handful for this.
